This interactive explorer is the detailed companion to the report's increment-based
summary graphs. The slider evaluates every integer n from 2 through 500 using the
same four normality criteria and the same 10,000-repetition simulation design.

## Interactive explorer

Move the slider to inspect a specific sample size, or choose a graph type to change
the evidence shown below.

```{=html}
<div id="clt-explorer" class="clt-explorer"
     data-url="assets/full-grid-visuals.json">
  <div class="explorer-controls">
    <label class="explorer-control">
      <span>Population</span>
      <select id="clt-population" aria-label="Choose a population"></select>
    </label>

    <label class="explorer-control">
      <span>Graph type</span>
      <select id="clt-graph" aria-label="Choose a graph type">
        <option value="histogram">Sampling distribution</option>
        <option value="qq">Normal Q-Q plot</option>
        <option value="diagnostics">Diagnostic thresholds</option>
        <option value="comparison">All populations at this n</option>
      </select>
    </label>

    <label class="explorer-control explorer-slider">
      <span>Sample size <output id="clt-n-output">30</output></span>
      <input id="clt-n" type="range" min="2" max="500" step="1" value="30"
             aria-label="Choose sample size">
      <span class="explorer-range"><span>n = 2</span><span>n = 500</span></span>
    </label>
  </div>

  <div id="clt-loading" class="explorer-loading" role="status">
    Loading precomputed simulation evidence…
  </div>
  <div id="clt-error" class="explorer-error" role="alert" hidden></div>

  <div class="explorer-summary">
    <div id="clt-status" class="explorer-status">Loading…</div>
    <p id="clt-stable" class="explorer-stable"></p>
    <p id="clt-description" class="explorer-description"></p>
  </div>

  <div id="clt-metrics" class="explorer-metrics" aria-live="polite"></div>
  <svg id="clt-plot" class="explorer-plot"
       role="img" aria-label="Interactive simulation graph"></svg>
</div>

<script src="assets/full-grid-explorer.js"></script>
```

## How to interpret the explorer

- **Sampling distribution** shows the simulated distribution of the 10,000 sample
  means at the selected n.
- **Normal Q-Q plot** compares standardized simulated quantiles with theoretical
  normal quantiles. Points closer to the dashed diagonal indicate closer agreement.
- **Diagnostic thresholds** shows the four numerical criteria as criterion-load
  bars. A bar ending at or before the orange boundary passes that criterion.
- **All populations at this n** compares the pass/fail screen across every
  population at the selected integer.

The status badge refers to the exact selected integer. The “first stable pass”
line refers to the first n followed by two additional consecutive passing
integers.

::: {.callout-note}
The interactive page uses one reproducible simulation path per population and
cumulative sums to make every integer n available efficiently. Because the
primary candidate-grid experiments reset the seed separately for each candidate,
small Monte Carlo differences between the two views are expected. The diagnostic
criteria and stable-pass rule are unchanged.
:::

## Reproduce the interactive data

From the repository root:

```bash
Rscript R/run_full_grid.R
Rscript R/run_interactive_data.R
quarto render full-grid.qmd --no-clean --cache-refresh
```

The compact visual data are saved to
`results/tables/full_grid_visuals.json` and copied to
`docs/assets/full-grid-visuals.json` for the published site. The interactive
JavaScript is maintained in `assets/full-grid-explorer.js`.
